REPLACE-CHECK

The check passes today with no warnings in `-W error::DeprecationWarning` mode, yet the second run without that flag shows the 2 warnings still exist. This means the check cannot discriminate "done" from "untouched" — the warning is already filtered at error level but still emitted at default level. The criterion asks that the tests "SHALL NOT emit" the warning, but the check only catches warnings promoted to errors; a proper check would verify the warnings summary is clean (e.g., `pytest ... -q 2>&1 | grep -c DeprecationWarning` returns 0, or the run shows "0 warnings").
